quote: Viel- leicht kommt beides auf dasselbe hinaus, vergl. meinen Brief an Klein vom 15 Dec. 1894.
english: Perhaps both come to the same thing; compare my letter to Klein of 15 Dec. 1894.
topic: The page ends a number-theoretic argument, asks how the quadratic extension obtained from the roots of a cubic equation relates to the cubic base field, and sets out a plan to apply the ideal concept to all mathematical disciplines, as Lie did with the group concept.

triage.modern_statement: The first part of the question can be pinned down. Take a non-Galois cubic field K = Q(θ) with discriminant d. Adjoining all the roots of the cubic gives its Galois closure N = K(√d), which is a quadratic extension of K and a dihedral (S3) field of degree 6. Hilbert asks how this quadratic extension N/K relates to the cubic base field K. In modern terms that is about splitting, ramification and the class group of N/K, and about the link through class field theory to unramified cyclic cubic extensions of Q(√d). The conjecture itself, 'perhaps both come to the same thing', compares two notions or constructions that are not named in the excerpt. The note refers to his letter to Klein of 15 Dec. 1894 for the details. That letter is printed in G. Frei (ed.), Der Briefwechsel David Hilbert – Felix Klein (1985), but I could not find its text online. Without it, I cannot say what the two things being equated are.
triage.answered_by: Cannot be determined. The two notions Hilbert says 'come to the same thing' are only described in the 15 Dec. 1894 letter to Klein, which I could not access. The general topic, how the Galois closure of a cubic field relates to the cubic field and to the quadratic field Q(√d), was later worked out by class field theory (Hilbert, Furtwängler, Takagi, Hasse). This is standard background and is not confirmed as the answer to this specific note.

evidence.claim: The Hilbert–Klein correspondence (1886–1918), which would contain the 15 Dec. 1894 letter, was edited by Günther Frei and published in 1985.
Hilbert and Klein were exchanging research letters in 1894. For example, his letter of 14 Aug. 1894 is the origin of Hilbert geometry, which shows the letters carried mathematical content.
Modern background, not a resolution of this note: the Galois closure N of a non-Galois cubic field L is a dihedral field of degree 6 containing a unique quadratic field K.
Modern background, not a resolution of this note: by class field theory, non-Galois cubic fields with discriminant d correspond to unramified cyclic cubic extensions of Q(√d).

triage.why: The note says only that 'both' (beides) might come to the same thing. What the two items are is in a letter I could not reach through search. The page context places it in the theory of relative quadratic fields over a cubic field, which Hilbert was working on around the time of the Zahlbericht (1894–97). That area was later absorbed into class field theory, and the dihedral/cubic correspondence is now standard. But I cannot confirm that this is what Hilbert's conjecture meant or say whether it was proved. It is not one of the 23 problems or the 24th problem, although the subject is close to the 9th and 12th problems. Checking the 15 Dec. 1894 letter in Frei (1985) would settle it.
